Q: Getting error every time Error: Permission denied @ rb_file_s_rename on linkage.json A:

I received a similar error:

Error: Permission denied @ rb_file_s_rename - (/usr/local/var/homebrew/tmp/.cellar/readline/8.3.3, /usr/local/Cellar/readline/8.3.3)

I ran the following:

sudo chown -R $(whom):admin /usr/local/Cellar

and I was able to install what I needed.

Q: Cause: zip END header not found A:

I was on Windows when this happened. I'm not sure what fixed it exactly, but a combination of deleting .gradle, adding the folder to the Windows Defender Exclusion list (it's a prompt you have to accept that shows up when you open the project in Android Studio 4.0), and clicking the elephant icon in the upper right hand corner (which syncs the project with Gradle files) solved the issue for me.

Q: How to override quarkus profile when running failsafe integration tests A:

You can’t reliably override quarkus.profile in Failsafe if it was already set at build time, because Quarkus detects it as a duplicate system property and keeps the first one.

The fix is to avoid setting quarkus.profile during the Maven build (mvn install -Dquarkus.profile=qa). Instead, set the profile only when running tests:

mvn verify -Dquarkus.profile=IT

or define it inside the Failsafe plugin using <systemPropertyVariables>.

Also avoid using argLine to override it, because it will still conflict if the property is already defined elsewhere.

Q: Conversion IP private to IP public for find location A: 
import requests

try:
    # 1. Grab your real public IP address instantly
    public_ip = requests.get('https://api.ipify.org').text
    print(f"Your Public IP Address is: {public_ip}")
    
    # 2. Query a free geolocation service with that public IP
    geo_data = requests.get(f'https://ipapi.co/{public_ip}/json/').json()
    
    # 3. Print out your location details
    print(f"City: {geo_data.get('city')}")
    print(f"Region: {geo_data.get('region')}")
    print(f"Country: {geo_data.get('country_name')}")
    
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error fetching location: {e}")

Q: How can I efficiently delete expired records in PostgreSQL? A:

Scheduled job is a safe place to start. Sometimes you just can't predict these things, so go with the simple and obvious solution first. Forget trying to predict the future. You can't.

Make it easy. Make it fast. Fix it, if it becomes an issue.

That's how we do it.
